questions.question: Who among the following list of Prime Ministers has NOT been awarded Bharat Ratna?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following list of Prime Ministers has NOT been awarded Bharat Ratna?
questions.solution:
Except for V.P.Singh, who served as Prime Minister of India from 1989-1990, other above mentioned Prime Ministers have been awarded Bharat Ratna. Added to that, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi has also been awarded Bharat Ratna.

Bharat Ratna was first constituted in the year 1954. The award is conferred in recognition of exceptional service/performance of the highest order. It is the highest civilian award of India. Recipients receive a Sanad signed by the President and a peepal-leaf - shaped medallion.

questions.question: Who is the first woman Nobel prize laureate?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the first woman Nobel prize laureate?
questions.solution: The first woman to receive a Nobel Prize was Marie Curie, who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903. She was also the first person to be awarded two Nobel Prizes, the second award being the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, given in 1911. She is also the only female laurate to awarded twice out of 48 female laurate.

questions.question: Who was the first recipient of Man Booker Prize?
questions.questionHtml: Who was the first recipient of Man Booker Prize?
questions.solution:
P. H. Newby was the first recipient of the award in 1969 for his novel "Something to Answer For". He was also a broadcasting administrator. His first novel, "A Journey into the Interior".

The Man Booker Prize was established in 1969. It is a literary prize awarded each year for the best original novel, written in the English language and published in the UK. The winner receives ≤50,000 as well as the ≤2,500 awarded to each of the shortlisted authors. Both the winner and the shortlisted authors are guaranteed a worldwide readership plus an increase in book sales.

questions.question: Pulitzer Prize is associated with which among the following field?
questions.questionHtml: Pulitzer Prize is associated with which among the following field?
questions.solution: The award is presented for achievements in the field of newspaper, magazine and online journalism, literature, and musical composition in the United States. The award comprises 21 categories. The awards are presented in memory of Newspaper publisher Joseph Pulitzer.

questions.question: The first edition of International Film Festival of India (IFFI) was held in which year?
questions.questionHtml: The first edition of International Film Festival of India (IFFI) was held in which year?
questions.solution: The 1st edition of IFFI was in the year 1952. The IFFI aims at providing a common platform for the cinemas of the world to project the excellence of the film art. It aims to contribute to the understanding and appreciation of film cultures of different nations and promoting friendship and cooperation among people of the world.

questions.question: Rabindranath Tagore received Nobel Prize for literature in which year?
questions.questionHtml: Rabindranath Tagore received Nobel Prize for literature in which year?
questions.solution: The Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to Rabindranath Tagore in the year 1913. He was the first Indian and first non- European to receive Nobel Prize in literature. He is referred to as "the Bard of Bengal". He is the composer of national anthem of India and Bangladesh.

questions.question: Which among the following is referred to as Green Noble?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following is referred to as Green Noble?
questions.solution: The Goldman Environmental Prize honors grassroots environmental heroes. The aim is to inspire other ordinary people to take extraordinary actions to protect the natural world. It was established in 1989 and is given by the Goldman Environmental Foundation. It is given to persons, one from each of the world's six geographic regions: Africa, Asia, Europe, Islands and Island Nations, North America, and South and Central America.

questions.question: International President's Award is presented by which among the following organisation?
questions.questionHtml: International President's Award is presented by which among the following organisation?

options.text: International Committee of the Red Cross
options.html: International Committee of the Red Cross

questions.solution: It is presented by WWF. International President's Award aims to recognise young people who are already active in conserving the natural environment, achieving significant success and/or innovative approaches, and whose efforts are influencing and inspiring others.

questions.question: "Nehru Award" is administered by which among the following Institution/Organization?
questions.questionHtml: "Nehru Award" is administered by which among the following Institution/Organization?

options.text: Centre for Cultural Resources and Training
options.html: Centre for Cultural Resources and Training

options.text: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education
options.html: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education

questions.solution: Nehru award is administered by Indian Council for Cultural Relations. It is given for outstanding contribution to the promotion of international understanding, goodwill, and friendship among peoples of the world. It is open to all persons regardless of nationality, race, creed or sex. It was first instituted in the year 1965.

questions.question: Award for Exceptional Bravery at Sea is presented by which organization/Institution?
questions.questionHtml: Award for Exceptional Bravery at Sea is presented by which organization/Institution?
questions.solution:
Award for Exceptional Bravery at Sea is presented by International Maritime Organization. This annual award was established by the Organization to provide international recognition for those who, at the risk of losing their own life, perform acts of exceptional bravery, displaying outstanding courage in attempting to save life at sea or in attempting to prevent or mitigate damage to the marine environment.

Captain Radhika Menon of Indian Merchant Navy was the recipient of 2016 award.

questions.question: Who is the author of Panchatantra?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the author of Panchatantra?
questions.solution: Panchatantra is an ancient Indian collection of interrelated animal fables written by Vishnu Sharma. It has been translated into many middle eastern and European languages.

questions.question: Who among the following coauthored with A.P.J Abdul Kalam the book "India 2020"?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following coauthored with A.P.J Abdul Kalam the book "India 2020"?
questions.solution: India 2020 was written by Dr.A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and coauthored by Dr. Y.S. Rajan. Dr. Rajan is an professor, scientist and administrator. The book was initially prepared as a document by Department of Science and Technology under the chairmanship of A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighter is the author of "Unhappy India"?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following freedom fighter is the author of "Unhappy India"?
questions.solution:
Unhappy India was written by Lala Lajpat Rai. It was published in the year 1928. It deals with the poor condition of India and her people under British rule.

Lala Lajpat Rai was popularly known as Punjab Kesari. He was also the founder of Punjab National Bank.

questions.question: Which among the following was NOT authored by kalidas?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following was NOT authored by kalidas?
questions.solution: Rajtarangini was written in Sanskrit by Kashmiri historian Kalhana. It talks about the culture, food and dressing sense of people of Kashmir region and the relations of Kashmir with its neighbors. The rest of the works mentioned above were written by Kalidas, who served as court poet in Gupta empire.

questions.question: Who is the author of Neither a Hawk nor a dove?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the author of Neither a Hawk nor a dove?
questions.solution: The book was written by Khurshid Mahmud Kasuri. It gives a comprehensive account by a Pakistani Foreign Minister who contributed in moving the peace process with India forward. It provides a detailed analysis of the Kashmir issue and the complex Pakistan-US-Afghanistan-India quadrangular relationship.

questions.question: Who among the following author has written a biography on former PM Lal Bahadur Shastri?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following author has written a biography on former PM Lal Bahadur Shastri?
questions.solution: Lal Bahadur Shastri: Lessons in Leadership, a biography on Former PM Lal Bahadur Shastri was written by Pavan Choudary. This book carries anecdotes encapsulating Lal Bahadur's childhood, growing up years and political life. Each anecdote is poignantly narrated by his son Anil Shastri.

questions.question: Who authored the book "My Country My Life"?
questions.questionHtml: Who authored the book "My Country My Life"?
questions.solution: My Country My Life is an autobiographical book by L. K. Advani. This book covers, chronologically, most of all the major and minor events in the life of the author. The book alongside mentions the event in Indian politics and India's history from 1900 till date.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book "Mrs Funny Bones"?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the author of the book "Mrs Funny Bones"?
questions.solution: Mrs Funnybones: She's Just Like You and a Lot Like Me is a 2015 Indian non-fiction book written by former film actress Twinkle Khanna. The book is a collection of anecdotes wherein the author shows the hilarious aspect of our everyday lives and especially the glimpse of a modern working woman.

questions.question: Born again on the mountain is an autobiography of who among the following?
questions.questionHtml: Born again on the mountain is an autobiography of who among the following?
questions.solution: The book was written by Arunima Sinha. She is the first female amputee (and the first Indian amputee) to climb Mount Everest. The book was launched by Prime minister of India Narendra Modi.

questions.question: Which of the following literary works if the first to make reference to puppet theatre?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following literary works if the first to make reference to puppet theatre?
questions.solution: The earliest reference to the art of puppetry is found in Tamil classic 'Silappadikaaram' written around the 1st or 2nd century B.C. Natyashastra makes reference to the producer-cum-director of the human theatre as 'Sutradhar'. Added to this, Srimad Bhagavata, also talks about puppetry. It says that Lord Krishna with three strings-Satta, Raja and Tama, the God manipulates each object in the universe as a marionette.

questions.question: Which among the following festival is celebrated in Meghalaya?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following festival is celebrated in Meghalaya?
questions.solution: Wangala festival is celebrated by tribes of Garo hills in Meghalaya. It is an age-old practice by the 'Songsareks' or non-Christian Garos in all the villages of Garo Hills, celebrated at every harvesting period in late autumn. The first "Hundred Drums Wangala Festival" was organised in the year 1976 to protect the culture of garo tribes.

questions.question: Satrriya dance originated in which state?
questions.questionHtml: Satrriya dance originated in which state?
questions.solution: It is a classical dance from the state of Assam. The Sattriya dance form was introduced in the 15th century A.D by the great Vaishnava saint and reformer of Assam, Mahapurusha Sankaradeva as a powerful medium for propagation of the Vaishnava faith. It incorporates different elements from various treatises, local folk dances with his own rare outlook.

questions.question: Rasiaya Geet is a tradition of which state?
questions.questionHtml: Rasiaya Geet is a tradition of which state?
questions.solution: Tradition of singing Rasiaya Geet is in the state of Uttar Pradesh. 'Rasiya' word is derived from the word rasa (emotion) because rasiya means that which is filled with rasa or emotion. It reflects the personality of the singer as well as the nature of the song.

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a regional music of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following is NOT a regional music of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution: Laman is associated with Himachal Pradesh. In Laman a group of girls sing a stanza and a group of boys give reply in the song. This continues for hours. Interesting is that the girls singing on one of the peaks of the hill seldom see the faces of the boys singing on another peak. In between is the hill which echoes their love song. Most of these songs are sung especially in Kullu Valley.

questions.question: "Villu Pattu" folk music is related to which state?
questions.questionHtml: "Villu Pattu" folk music is related to which state?
questions.solution: Villu Pattu is a popular folk music of Tamil Nadu. The lead singer also plays the role of the main performer. He also handles the dominating instrument which is bow shaped. The songs revolve around theological themes and the conquest of good over evil is emphasised.

questions.question: The book "Sangeeth Sudhraka" was written by who among the following?
questions.questionHtml: The book "Sangeeth Sudhraka" was written by who among the following?
questions.solution: The book was written by Haripala. It deals with classical musics, namely Carnatic and Hindustani. The terms Carnatic and Hindustani are found for the first time in this book. Other treatises on music are the Natya shastra of Bharata Muni, Brihaddesi of Matanga, Sangeeta Ratnakara of Sharangadeva.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT a part of Trinity of Carnatic music?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following is NOT a part of Trinity of Carnatic music?
questions.solution: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri are referred to as Trinity of Carnatic Music. Dynamic development in Carnatic music took place in their era. The Trinity were not only contemporaries among themselves but, also contemporaries of great composers of Western Music, as Beethoven, Mozart, Wagner and Haydn. It was the 'Golden Age' of music throughout the world. Carnatic music reached its pinnacle of artistic excellence during this period.

questions.question: Pancha Ratha temples are found in which among the following places?
questions.questionHtml: Pancha Ratha temples are found in which among the following places?
questions.solution: Pancha Rathas is a monolithic Indian rock-cut architecture in Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu. It has been accorded UNESCO World Heritage site status. These include the Dharmaraja Ratha, Bhima Ratha, Arjuna Ratha, Nakula Sahadeva Ratha, and Draupadi Ratha.

questions.question: Bhavai is a folk drama of which state?
questions.questionHtml: Bhavai is a folk drama of which state?
questions.solution: It is a folk drama of Gujarat. It is a continuous performance lasting the whole night. Women are not allowed to take part in the Bhavai. Therefore, the male artists perform female roles. The topics on which Bhavais are prepared are taken from the life of common man.
